notes.b: Before splitting fitness into types, you need to know what health and fitness each mean, because the two words are not interchangeable. Fitness is only one part of health.
points: Health, as defined by the World Health Organization (the United Nations health agency): a state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity (weakness or frailty).
Health is broader than fitness, because it includes mental and social well-being as well as the body. So a person can be fit for their sport but unwell, or healthy but unfit.

Physical fitness: the ability to carry out daily tasks and physical activity with vigour and without undue fatigue (without becoming more tired than the task justifies), with energy left to meet emergencies.

The specification names four demands of performance, the things an athlete must get right: health-related fitness, performance-related fitness, psychological preparation (getting the mind ready), and diet and nutrition. Each has its own notes in this chapter.
notes.tip: Quote the World Health Organization definition and make the point that health is broader than fitness, since mental and social well-being count as well as the physical.

notes.b: Physical fitness is made up of separate components, and the specification sorts them into two lists: those that serve health and those that serve sporting success. You should be able to list both and place any component in the right one.
points: Health-related fitness (HRF): the components linked to good health and a lower risk of disease that everyone needs for daily life.

The HRF components are cardio-respiratory endurance (how long the heart and lungs can keep the body working), muscular endurance (how long a muscle can keep working), strength (the most force a muscle can produce), flexibility (range of movement at a joint) and body composition (the proportions of fat and other tissue in the body). Strength sits here, not under PRF.

Performance-related fitness (PRF), also called skill-related fitness: the components needed for successful performance in sport. They are agility (changing direction quickly), balance (staying steady), co-ordination (moving body parts smoothly together), power (force applied quickly), speed (how fast you move) and reaction time (how fast you respond to a signal).
Classifying a component: co-ordination, agility and reaction time are PRF; muscular endurance, flexibility and strength are HRF.
notes.tip: Strength is health-related and power is performance-related, so do not move them. Questions ask you to classify named components as HRF or PRF, sometimes in a table with test results, so learn both lists exactly. Here, list the components only and do not define each one at length.

notes.h: Differences between health-related and performance-related fitness
notes.b: The two categories differ in why you need them, who needs them, how far training can change them and how you build them. These four contrasts are the answer when you are asked to discuss the difference.
points: Purpose: HRF supports health and the demands of daily living, whereas PRF supports the demands of a particular sport or activity.
Who needs it: everyone needs HRF, because everyone has daily tasks to carry out. PRF matters mainly to performers, and which components matter depends on the activity.

Trainability (how far training can improve it): HRF responds well to training for most people. PRF is more strongly influenced by genetics (the abilities a person inherits) and is more specific to the activity.

How it is developed: HRF through general exercise such as running, swimming and resistance work (training against a load, such as weights). PRF mainly through sport-specific drills and practice, which repeat the movements of that sport.
notes.tip: When asked to discuss the difference, as in an Ordinary Level question after you name three components, give contrasts on purpose, who needs it, trainability and how it is developed, rather than just defining each type.

notes.h: Is health-related fitness the same as performance-related fitness?
notes.b: This is a statement you may be asked to evaluate. The answer is that it is inaccurate, but the two types of fitness are linked, and a good answer says both.
points: The statement is inaccurate, because the two differ in purpose, in who needs them, in how trainable they are and in how they are developed.
They are linked, however: a performer needs both, and many sports demand a high level of an HRF component, such as cardio-respiratory endurance for a Gaelic football midfielder.
Good HRF also supports PRF: strength underpins power, because power is force applied quickly, and flexibility helps agility.
notes.tip: To discuss the accuracy of this statement, say it is inaccurate and give the reasons from the differences above, then show that the two are linked. A Higher Level question has asked this.

keyTerms.definition: A state of complete physical, mental and social well-being and not merely the absence of disease or infirmity (World Health Organization).
The ability to carry out daily tasks and physical activity with vigour and without undue fatigue.
The fitness components linked to good health that everyone needs: cardio-respiratory endurance, muscular endurance, strength, flexibility and body composition.
The fitness components needed for sporting performance: agility, balance, co-ordination, power, speed and reaction time.

questions.prompt: 'Health-related fitness is the same as performance-related fitness.' Discuss the accuracy of this statement.
questions.model: The statement is not accurate. Health-related fitness (cardio-respiratory endurance, muscular endurance, strength, flexibility, body composition) is needed by everyone for health and daily living, while performance-related fitness (agility, balance, co-ordination, power, speed, reaction time) is needed for success in sport. HRF responds well to training, whereas PRF is more influenced by genetics and specific to the activity. However, they overlap: a Gaelic football midfielder needs high cardio-respiratory endurance (HRF) as well as speed and agility (PRF), and strength underpins power.

questions.prompt: Name three components of physical fitness and state whether each is health-related or performance-related.
questions.model: Flexibility: health-related. Agility: performance-related. Muscular endurance: health-related.
